name: Selective IgA Deficiency

prevalence.estimate: 1 in 300 to 1 in 700 in Caucasian populations

ethnicAssociations: Rare in Asian populations (1 in 5,000-18,000 in Japan)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ESID Diagnostic Criteria for Selective IgA Deficiency

criteria.description: Serum IgA level <7 mg/dL (0.07 g/L) in a patient older than 4 years
Normal serum levels of IgG and IgM
Exclusion of other causes of hypogammaglobulinemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Undetectable serum IgA (<7 mg/dL) with normal IgG and IgM in a patient >4 years old, after exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Partial IgA deficiency (IgA detectable but >2 SD below mean) is more common but less clinically significant. Most patients are asymptomatic and discovered incidentally. ~10% may progress to CVID.

common.notes: Most individuals with selective IgA deficiency are clinically silent

searchTerms: common allergies such as skin rash and breathing problems

occasional.notes: 10-15 fold increased risk of celiac disease
searchTerms: conditions like lupus or rheumatoid arthritis

rare.notes: Severe anaphylaxis to blood products containing IgA; occurs in patients who develop anti-IgA antibodies
searchTerms: severe allergic reaction to blood transfusion

rare.notes: ~5-10% may evolve to CVID over years
searchTerms: development of common variable immune deficiency

rare.symptomName: Nodular lymphoid hyperplasia of GI tract
searchTerms: small lumps of immune tissue in gut

laboratory: Normal serum IgG and IgM levels
Normal specific antibody responses to vaccines (usually)
Anti-IgA antibodies may be present (class-specific or subclass-specific)
Screen for celiac disease (anti-tissue transglutaminase IgG, since IgA-based tests will be false negative)
imaging: CT chest if recurrent lower respiratory infections
genetic: HLA associations: HLA-A1, HLA-B8, HLA-DR3 haplotype
Shared genetic susceptibility with CVID (same family)
Usually sporadic; occasionally autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
other: IgA typing should be repeated to confirm persistence
Anti-IgA antibody testing before blood transfusions

distinguishingFeatures: CVID has low IgG plus low IgA and/or IgM
More symptomatic with recurrent serious infections
Normal B cell numbers and function
Temporal association with medications (phenytoin, sulfasalazine, gold)

redFlags: Anaphylactic reaction to blood transfusion (anti-IgA antibody mediated)
Development of progressive hypogammaglobulinemia suggesting evolution to CVID
Recurrent severe sinopulmonary infections with bronchiectasis
Coexistent celiac disease (should be screened for)
specialistType: Transfusion Medicine Specialist (for safe blood product selection)
